systems.name: Vercel Geist
systems.what: Vercel's design system. Geist Sans and Geist Mono, a grey-first palette, and colour scales where every step has one job.
systems.font: Geist Sans, with Geist Mono for code and labels
systems.scaleNote: Geist names each style by its size: text-heading-72 down to text-heading-14, then label, copy and button styles.

ramp.note: Structure, drawn in grey. Ten scales (gray, gray-alpha, blue, red, amber, green, teal, purple, pink) share these ten steps.

steal.text: Name styles by their size and role (heading-32, copy-16, label-13). Nobody has to guess what 'h3' means.
Ten steps per colour, each with one job: 100 to 300 backgrounds, 400 to 600 borders, 700 to 800 solid fills, 900 to 1000 text.
Keep space in a small set of steps and let grey borders, not boxes of colour, separate things.
Quiet, short transitions on hover and open. Motion confirms an action; it never performs.
Default, hover and active are neighbouring steps on the same scale, so every state is one step away.

systems.toolkit: I set my greys as ten role-named steps with the oklch picker, then wire them into shadcn's CSS variables.

systems.name: Linear
systems.what: Linear's dark, dense app UI. Its 2024 redesign turned 98 hand-set theme variables into three inputs, generated in the LCH colour space.
systems.font: Inter Display for headings, Inter for everything else
systems.scaleNote: I haven't checked Linear's exact sizes, so I don't draw them. What Linear documents is the pairing: Inter Display for headings, Inter for the dense UI.

steal.text: Use two cuts of one family: a tighter display cut for headings and the plain one for dense UI.
Generate a theme from three inputs (base, accent, contrast) instead of hand-picking every surface.
Density is a feature. Tight rows, aligned edges and less chrome let more content fit without noise.
Fast and small. Panels and menus arrive quickly and never block the next keypress.
Elevation and hover come from opacities of black and white, so they work on any generated theme.

systems.toolkit: I pick base and accent with the oklch picker (LCH's close cousin), then set hover and elevation as white at low opacity.

systems.name: Stripe
systems.what: Stripe's marketing site and its UI toolkit for apps. A strict column grid, calm type, and colour that only moves where it means something.
systems.font: A clean grotesk for text; described, not measured
systems.scaleNote: I have not verified Stripe's exact sizes, so I don't draw them. The lesson is the grid: every section sits on the same column lines.

steal.text: Few sizes, used strictly. Headlines carry the energy, body text stays quiet and readable.
A living gradient carries the brand, while the UI around it stays white, grey and one accent.
A visible column grid (the Connect page even draws its stripes with CSS Grid) keeps dense pages calm.
Only transform and opacity, mostly under 500ms, started when it scrolls into view.
Pick the lightest tool that works: CSS first, the Web Animations API next, a library last.

systems.toolkit: I build the gradient with ShaderGradient or Paper Shaders and keep the rest of the page on GSAP with transform and opacity only.

systems.name: Apple HIG
systems.what: Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Rules for every Apple platform, built on San Francisco and Dynamic Type, where text sizes follow the reader's settings.
systems.font: San Francisco (SF Pro), sized by Dynamic Type
systems.scaleNote: iOS text styles at the default Large setting, in points. Headline is also 17, set semibold.

steal.text: Name styles by purpose (Title, Body, Footnote), not by size, so they can all grow together.
System colours adapt to light, dark and high contrast. Ask for 'label' or 'secondary label', not a hex.
Hit targets at least 44 by 44 points, even when the icon is smaller.
Motion should explain where things came from, and it respects the Reduce Motion setting.
Every control has clear pressed, disabled and focused looks that don't rely on colour alone.

systems.toolkit: I set type in rem so it follows the reader's settings, and run the Web Interface Guidelines skill to check hit sizes and reduced motion.

systems.name: Material 3
systems.what: Google's design system. Fifteen named text styles, colour roles made from one source colour, and state layers for every interaction.
systems.font: Roboto by default; any family can fill the roles
systems.scaleNote: Seven of the fifteen styles (display, headline, title, body, label, each large, medium and small), from the material-web tokens.

steal.text: Five roles times three sizes. Fifteen styles is enough for any app, and each has a clear job.
Roles come in pairs: every 'primary' has an 'on-primary' for the text on top, so contrast is designed in.
A 4dp grid with shape tokens for corner radius, from none to full.
Easing and duration are tokens too, so every transition in the app feels related.
A state layer: the content colour laid over the surface at 8% on hover, 12% on focus and press, 16% on drag.

systems.toolkit: I copy the state-layer idea into Tailwind: one hover overlay at 8%, one pressed at 12%, and ease tokens picked on easings.net.

systems.name: Radix + shadcn
systems.what: Radix gives accessible primitives and 12-step colour scales. shadcn/ui gives you the component code itself, styled with a short list of CSS variables.
systems.font: Whatever you choose; shadcn doesn't set a type scale
systems.scaleNote: No type scale here on purpose. Radix and shadcn own colour, behaviour and states, and leave type to you.

ramp.note: Radix Colors: twelve steps per scale, each step with a job. Drawn in grey.

steal.text: Keep type out of the component library, so one kit fits many brands.
Pair every surface with a '-foreground' variable. Swap the variables and the whole kit re-themes.
One --radius variable sets every corner, so the whole kit changes shape at once.
Primitives expose open and closed states as data attributes, so you animate them with plain CSS.
Focus is a --ring variable and keyboard behaviour comes from Radix, so accessible states come free.

systems.toolkit: I add components with the shadcn CLI, then set the variables from my own token sheet instead of the default zinc.

systems.name: Win95 / BR95
systems.what: My Windows 95 token sheet. Grey bevels, pixel fonts and a black title bar, used in the opening act of this site.
systems.font: MS Sans Serif pixel, with IBM VGA 8x16 for labels
systems.scaleNote: Pixel sizes stay on the 8x16 grid: 16, 32, 48, 64.

steal.text: Pixel fonts only at multiples of 16px, with font smoothing off, so every pixel stays sharp.
Six greys do everything. The classic teal and navy are swapped for grey and black.
Measured numbers from the real thing: an 18px title bar and a 28px taskbar.
Stepped, not eased. Windows jump like it's 1995.
Pressed is the bevel flipped: the four inset shadows swap light and dark.

systems.toolkit: I build the chrome by hand in CSS and check it frame by frame with the Playwright MCP.

systems.name: Black and white
systems.what: The default look of this site. Near-black ground, seven greys, a pixel font for labels and a serif for big headings.
systems.font: Newsreader for display, Schibsted Grotesk for reading, IBM VGA 8x16 for labels
systems.scaleNote: Reading text is 17px at 1.6 line height, at most 68 characters wide.

steal.text: Three voices with three jobs: pixel for labels, serif for big moments, sans for reading.
Seven greys, never raw hex in a component. Even the dimmest label passes AA on the ground.
Hairline borders and 1px gaps between tiles do the separating, not shadows.
Every scroll animation sits inside a reduced-motion check. Reduced motion gets the final state at once.
Hover lifts a surface one grey step (line to steel). Focus is a visible outline, always.

systems.toolkit: I keep these as CSS variables in one file, and let GSAP and Lenis move things on top of them.

systems.name: Colour
systems.what: The finale sheet. Six loud hues that arrive one at a time, then all at once.
systems.font: Same families as black and white; the colour does the shouting
systems.scaleNote: Text on colour is always #080808 or #ffffff, whichever passes 4.5:1.

steal.text: Don't add sizes for the colour act. Colour is already loud; the type stays the same.
Six hues, each saturated to the edge, and nothing in between.
Colour goes full bleed. A small swatch of a loud colour looks like a mistake; a whole field looks like a choice.
Introduce colour gradually: one hue in one piece, then fields, then everything.
On colour, text is only black or white, picked by contrast, never a tint.

systems.toolkit: I test each pair for 4.5:1 with the oklch picker and paint the fields with Paper Shaders.
